one_liner: Slack has a broad, mature REST Web API with OAuth 2.0 self-serve app registration, a free developer sandbox, and an official hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: Users are sent through the OAuth 2.0 flow to obtain user/bot tokens; tokens are bearer tokens in the Authorization header. Bot/user tokens are also given at app creation for own workspace.
access_notes: Anyone can create a Slack app. The free Developer Program provides a sandbox with all Slack features at no cost. Workspace admin approval may be needed to install in other workspaces.
blocker_notes: None for building; a free developer sandbox and self-serve app creation are available.

evidence.quote: In order to obtain other users' tokens, you'll need to send users through the [OAuth 2.0 authentication flow](https://api.slack.com/authentication).
When creating an app for the first time, you'll be given your own user and bot token while going through the app creation process.

A developer sandbox is an Enterprise org environment (a network of two or more Slack workspace instances) that can be used to build against all Slack features safely and securely, without an additional cost.
Join the [Developer Program](https://api.slack.com/developer-program) and provision a sandbox with access to all Slack features for free.
[Slack API](/reference/methods) methods are accessible over HTTP, so the world is your oyster.
Since Slack hosts and manages the MCP Server, handling the tool logic on your behalf, implementing the connection is simple.
Slack only permits MCP on internal apps and directory-published apps, so an app built in your own workspace qualifies.
